name: Taiwan

nso.name: Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS), Executive Yuan (行政院主計總處)
nso.note: English site https://eng.dgbas.gov.tw/ ; the census results are served from a separate census portal, recalled as https://census.dgbas.gov.tw/ . Two other offices matter here: the Ministry of the Interior's Department of Household Registration (https://www.ris.gov.tw/, register statistics) and the Council of Indigenous Peoples (https://www.cip.gov.tw/).

latest_census.notes: The 2020 Population and Housing Census (109年人口及住宅普查, Nov-Dec 2020) is register-based with a sample survey. Taiwan's census has never had a religion item (recalled with reasonable confidence; the 2010 census certainly did not ask it). 'Ethnicity' here means indigenous status and tribe (原住民身分/族別), which the census carries from the household register; there is no Han/Hakka/Hoklo item. Language: the 2010 census (99年普查) asked 'languages used at home' (在家使用語言) for residents aged 6+, published as multi-response shares (Mandarin ~83.5%, Minnan ~81.9%, Hakka ~6.6%, indigenous ~1.4%) by county/city; I believe the 2020 census repeated the item but that is recalled with less confidence. Multi-response, so it is a Switzerland-style 'up to n languages per person' table, not a strict composition.

subnational_sources.title: Indigenous population by township/district (原住民人口數 by 鄉鎮市區, monthly household-registration statistics; also by tribe/族別)
subnational_sources.publisher: Ministry of the Interior, Department of Household Registration (內政部戶政司); mirrored by the Council of Indigenous Peoples
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled as a standing monthly series on the ris.gov.tw statistics pages (and on the CIP site), published as Excel/ODS. It counts indigenous persons (mountain/plains, and by the 16 recognised tribes) against total registered population, so what it yields is a two-part composition (indigenous vs. everyone else) with tribal detail inside the indigenous share -- a real count, but only a partial ethnicity composition. URL is the office homepage, not the table.

subnational_sources.title: 2010 Population and Housing Census -- languages used at home (在家使用語言) by county/city, residents aged 6 and over (multi-response)
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled: the 2010 census statistical tables were published as Excel on the DGBAS census portal, including a home-language table by county/city; 2020 likely repeats it. Multi-response (shares sum well over 100%), so it would need the Switzerland treatment (docs/SOURCES.md, 'up to three languages per person'). Whether a township-level breakdown exists is not known.

tier_reason: Counts exist (a register of indigenous status by all 368 townships; a census home-language table by 22 counties/cities, probably Excel), but the first is only a partial ethnicity composition and the second is multi-response, and neither URL is more than a homepage from memory. Religion is not asked by the census at all.
recommended_action: Crawl ris.gov.tw's monthly statistics for the indigenous-population-by-township workbook (Chinese column headers; 368 rows = admin2, 22 = admin1) and decide whether 'indigenous / non-indigenous (+ tribe)' is acceptable as an ethnicity composition. Then find the 2020 (else 2010) census home-language table on census.dgbas.gov.tw and load it as a multi-response language table if the Switzerland reader pattern fits. Declare religion not_collected at both levels: the census does not ask it and the MOI's religion statistics count temples and churches, not adherents.
not_found: Any adherent-level religion count by county (the MOI religion yearbook counts organisations, not people)
Any Han-subgroup (Hoklo/Hakka/mainlander) census item -- Hakka shares come from Hakka Affairs Council sample surveys, which are surveys and national/county estimates
Whether the 2020 census kept the home-language item and whether it is tabulated below county level
summary: Taiwan's census does not ask religion, and its only ethnicity item is indigenous status carried from the household register, so the realistic counts are the MOI's monthly indigenous-population-by-township workbook (368 townships = admin2, 22 counties/cities = admin1, Excel, a partial composition) and the 2010/2020 census 'languages used at home' table by county/city (multi-response). Tier B: real, public, probably machine-readable, but each needs a design decision before it is a composition. Religion should be declared not_collected.
